title: Sharp affine contraction for finite laws
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with mean zero. Suppose $q>2$ and $0<\lambda<1/2$, and that $X$ is supported almost everywhere on a finite set $S\subseteq\mathbb R$ such that $\mu(X=x)\ge\lambda$ for every $x\in S$. Then $X\in L^q(\mu)$, the radius $\rho=\sqrt{\sinh(u/q)/\sinh(u/(q/(q-1)))}$ with $u=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$ satisfies $0\le\rho<1$, and for all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, $\|a+\rho bX\|_{L^q(\mu)}\le\|a+bX\|_{L^2(\mu)}$.
hypotheses_covered: $X$ is almost surely supported on a finite set whose every listed value has probability at least $\lambda$
replaced: Let $q>2$, $0<\lambda<1/2$, and let $X$ be a centered measurable real random variable on a probability space, supported almost surely on a finite set whose atoms each have mass at least $\lambda$. Then $H_{2,q,\rho_*(q,\lambda)}(X)$ holds. Here $\rho_*(q,\lambda)=\sqrt{\sinh(\ell/q)/\sinh(\ell/(q/(q-1)))}$ with $\ell=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
